note: Field Config Cardinality overrides a field's cardinality per instance (per bundle). Core cardinality is a field-STORAGE property shared by all bundles; this module stores a per-instance override as the third-party setting field.field.<entity>.<bundle>.<field> -> third_party_settings.field_config_cardinality.cardinality_config (string: positive number, or -1 for unlimited), saved via the 'Allowed number of values (Cardinality Instance)' fieldset on field_config_edit_form. Enforcement is at render time (widget swaps of media_library_widget/image_image/entity_reference_autocomplete, provided widgets cardinality_email_default/cardinality_options_select/cardinality_ief_simple, and multi-value form alters). Medium/hard cases create namespaced content types fcc_* with a shared-storage (unlimited) field and read/write cardinality_config.

evals.prompt: In Drupal, cardinality is a field-storage property shared by every bundle. What does the field_config_cardinality module let you do about that, and where does it store the per-bundle override?
evals.expected_output: It lets you override cardinality per field instance (per bundle) so one shared field storage can be single-value on one bundle and multi-value on another. The override is stored as the third-party setting field.field.<entity>.<bundle>.<field> -> third_party_settings.field_config_cardinality.cardinality_config.

evals.prompt: How does field_config_cardinality actually enforce a lower per-instance cardinality in the edit form? Name at least one core field widget it replaces to do so.
evals.expected_output: In hook_field_widget_info_alter it swaps core widget classes for cardinality-aware subclasses - media_library_widget -> CardinalityMediaLibraryWidget, image_image -> CardinalityImageWidget, entity_reference_autocomplete -> CardinalityEntityReferenceAutocompleteWidget - and alters the multi-value form to cap value rows and drop the extra 'Add more' button.

evals.prompt: Where in the Drupal admin UI do I set a field_config_cardinality per-instance limit, and what is the fieldset called?
evals.expected_output: On the field instance edit form (Structure -> Content types -> <type> -> Manage fields -> <field> -> Edit, form field_config_edit_form). The module adds an 'Allowed number of values (Cardinality Instance)' fieldset where you pick Limited (+ a number) or Unlimited.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, content type 'fcc_m1' has a multi-value field 'field_fcc_m1' whose storage is unlimited, but field_config_cardinality overrides the per-instance limit. Inspect the live field configuration and state the per-instance cardinality limit for that field on fcc_m1.
evals.expected_output: The per-instance limit is 2: field.field.node.fcc_m1.field_fcc_m1 has third_party_settings.field_config_cardinality.cardinality_config = '2', even though the field storage is unlimited (-1).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the field 'field_fcc_m2' on content type 'fcc_m2' uses field_config_cardinality. Inspect the live configuration: is this instance limited to a single value, and which config key stores that limit?
evals.expected_output: Yes - the instance is limited to 1 value: field.field.node.fcc_m2.field_fcc_m2 has third_party_settings.field_config_cardinality.cardinality_config = '1'. The key that stores the per-instance limit is cardinality_config.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, content type 'fcc_h1' has a field 'field_fcc_h1' whose storage allows unlimited values. Using field_config_cardinality, limit THIS instance (on fcc_h1) to at most 3 values, without changing the shared field storage. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: On field.field.node.fcc_h1.field_fcc_h1 set third_party_settings.field_config_cardinality.cardinality_config to '3' (e.g. $fc->setThirdPartySetting('field_config_cardinality','cardinality_config','3')->save(), or Limited=3 in the 'Allowed number of values (Cardinality Instance)' fieldset). Verify checks cardinality_config === '3' while the storage stays unlimited.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, content type 'fcc_h2' has a field 'field_fcc_h2' with unlimited storage cardinality. Using field_config_cardinality, make this particular instance single-value (limit 1) without altering the field storage. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: On field.field.node.fcc_h2.field_fcc_h2 set third_party_settings.field_config_cardinality.cardinality_config to '1'. Verify checks cardinality_config === '1' while the storage stays unlimited.
